html:
Laws issued by the Spanish king Charles V in 1542 to protect Indigenous people in the Americas and limit the power of the conquistadors.

They followed decades of protest by friars, above all Bartolomé de las Casas, and built on the weaker Laws of Burgos of 1512. The main points:

  • Enslaving Indigenous people was banned.
  • No new encomiendas, grants of Indigenous labour and tribute, would be made.
  • Existing encomiendas would go back to the crown when their holders died, instead of passing to their children.
  • Officials and churchmen lost theirs at once.

Colonists were furious. In Peru, Gonzalo Pizarro, brother of Francisco Pizarro, led a revolt, and the viceroy was killed in battle in 1546. The crown backed down on inheritance in 1545, but the encomienda slowly faded anyway, replaced by other forms of forced labour such as the mita in Peru.
sum: Laws issued by the Spanish king Charles V in 1542 to protect Indigenous people in the Americas and limit the power of the conquistadors.
